artworks.title: Penelope and the Suitors
artworks.description: An oil on canvas (188 × 129.8 cm) by the English Pre-Raphaelite-influenced painter John William Waterhouse, now in Aberdeen Art Gallery (inv. ABDAG003035). The picture seizes on the central image of Penelope's long fidelity: seated at her great upright loom, the faithful wife of Odysseus works her weaving while a crowd of suitors presses in at the window, offering music, flowers and pleas. By day she weaves the funeral shroud for her father-in-law Laertes and by night unravels it, putting off her promise to choose a new husband and so keeping faith with the absent Odysseus through his twenty-year wandering. Waterhouse makes the loom a wall between her steadfast inward absorption and the importunate world outside.

artworks.title: Penelope recognizing the returned Odysseus (Roman fresco from the Macellum, Pompeii)
artworks.description: A Roman fresco from the Macellum, the central food market of Pompeii, buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79. The scene depicts the climactic homecoming of the Odyssey: Penelope, long besieged by suitors, confronts her husband Odysseus, who has returned to Ithaca disguised as a ragged beggar. The painting belongs to a popular Hellenistic-Roman repertoire of Odyssey episodes, prizing the moment of testing and recognition between the cautious queen and her unrecognized husband. It survives as one of the better-preserved ancient images of Penelope in the act that defined her in myth — the wary, intelligent wife who will not yield until she is certain.

artworks.title: Penelope (drawing after an antique vase)
artworks.description: A drawing by the French academic painter Adolphe Yvon (1817–1893), held in the Département des Arts Graphiques of the Louvre, rendering Penelope in the classical manner as 'a seated woman after the antique.' Yvon reprises one of the oldest visual formulas for Penelope, known from fifth-century Attic vase painting: the queen seated with her head bowed and a hand raised to her cheek in the attitude of grief and patient waiting, her loom nearby. The pose became the canonical image of mourning faithfulness, embodying the wife who endured Odysseus's twenty-year absence. Yvon's nineteenth-century copy testifies to the long afterlife of the ancient Penelope type in the academic tradition.

films.title: O Brother, Where Art Thou?
films.description: The Coens' Depression-era Odyssey gives Penelope a Mississippi double: Penny, the waiting wife who will not remarry until her wandering man comes home — loyalty restaged as screwball stubbornness.

films.title: The Odyssey
films.description: Konchalovsky's miniseries keeps Penelope at the loom and the bow-contest centre-stage — the Ithacan queen as the home the entire voyage is measured against.

films.title: Ulysses
films.description: Silvana Mangano's Penelope holds the Ithacan half of Camerini's epic — the shroud, the suitors and the recognition that ends Kirk Douglas' voyage.

films.title: The Return
films.description: Juliette Binoche's Penelope is the film's still centre — twenty years of ruled silence, then the hard choice to believe the beggar is her husband.

popCulture.title: Penelopean
popCulture.description: English borrowed the queen's name for faithful delay and endless weaving — a penelopean task is work undone each night so that hope can last another day.

popCulture.title: The Penelopiad
popCulture.creator: Margaret Atwood
popCulture.description: Atwood retells the Odyssey from the queen's side — and from the twelve hanged maids — turning Penelope's cleverness into a modern feminist myth.

popCulture.title: Ulysses
popCulture.creator: James Joyce
popCulture.description: Joyce ends his Dublin Odyssey with the 'Penelope' episode — Molly Bloom's unpunctuated night-thoughts as the modern queen's long, earthly yes.

music.title: Pénélope
music.description: Fauré's three-act poème lyrique gives the queen the opera: the loom, the suitors and the beggar's return scored as patient, luminous fidelity rather than Homeric blood.

music.title: Il ritorno d'Ulisse in patria
music.description: Monteverdi makes Penelope the opera's moral summit — her long refusal to hope, and the duet of recognition when the beggar strings the bow.

music.title: EPIC: The Musical
music.description: Rivera-Herrans' Odyssey musical keeps Penelope's songs as the Ithaca refrain — the queen waiting, weaving and finally choosing, saga by saga.
